correctness.rationale: At [1:-1:0:...:0], dehomogenize at x0 and put x1=-1+a, x2=b. The linear parts of f0 and f4 are -3b and 3a; their equations solve for a,b with order at least three, since the other terms not involving a,b are cubics. The remaining f1,f2,f3 divided by 3 start with u3*u6-u4*u7, u4*u8-u5*u6 and u5*u7-u3*u8. They are three independent minors of the stated two-row matrix. The rank-one ideal is prime of dimension four (Segre parametrization), so a larger initial ideal would have dimension at most three, contrary to the dimension-four local ring; completion preserves the associated graded. For uniformity, index the coordinates by the affine plane over F3. The projective Heisenberg stabilizer of the representative is exactly the order-three subgroup of phase characters agreeing at its two support sites: no nonidentity translation fixes a two-element support. Its Heisenberg orbit has 27 points. The normalizer preserves the invariant cubic space, and its Sp(4,F3) quotient acts transitively on the 40 lines of F3^4, giving 40 disjoint 27-point orbits distinguished by their stabilizers. This already exhausts the 1080 singular points of the cited primary classification. The graded dimensions (d+1)*binomial(d+2,2) sum to the claimed Hilbert series and give multiplicity 3; the three independent quadrics make all three formal generators minimal in height 2. On the blowup the projectivized cone is a smooth Cartier exceptional divisor: a local equation is a nonzerodivisor, and a regular quotient by that equation implies the total local ring is regular. The ideal of the divisor restricts to the Segre O(1), giving its normal O(-1,-1). The symbolic support file was inspected, not executed; the local computation was reconstructed directly and the global facts checked against arXiv:2611.16593v1. The geometric facts extend from characteristic-zero algebraically closed base changes of the rational equations. This is about blowing up the reduced points, not the Jacobian scheme or an analytic identification of germs.
